newsitem.title: UK: NWE GASOLINE PROMPT BARGES UP $3, SWAPS DOWN $4.
newsitem.headline: NWE GASOLINE PROMPT BARGES UP $3, SWAPS DOWN $4.

text.p: NWE gasoline levels were $3 higher on the prompt barge market at $237-$239 on Wednesday after suffering modest Nymex-led downward pressures from earlier strong gains.
Screen pressures left August mogas swap values $4.50 lower on the day as the cat cracker problems affecting first half August barges gave way to less bullish sentiments for the month as a whole.
Early premium unleaded barge deals at $240.25 - the highest level since the Gulf war - at $239 and $238 were followed by a pre-Nymex deal at $239, dealers said.
Talk activity in the $237-$238 range later was widely discounted.
Mogas swap trades were heard at $217.75 and $218 as two September trades were seen at $201.25 as well as a November deal at $187.
Sep/Oct was talked at $8, Oct/Nov at $3 and Nov/Dec at $1.50, and the August mogas/naphtha spread interest was earlier seen at $29.
Prompt to August 15 gasoline cargoes were rumoured offered at $240 CIF ARA, although second half August offers were heard as low as $235 and bids as far down as the high $220s.
